purpose: diagnose cupcake sensory defects to root cause across formula, mixing, bake, and ingredient, and drive a safe corrective-action loop toward the most delicious cupcake
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors grounded in canonical baking-science references

competency_questions.question: What sensory attributes are scored and on what scale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SENSORY_RUBRIC defines the 7 attributes and scale

competency_questions.question: How is assessor scoring kept reproducible across tasters?
What defects are in scope and how are they distinguished?
What is the non-defective crumb baseline?
What are the candidate root causes of a sunken center?
How are doming, cracking, and overflow distinguished from acceptable shape?
How is dryness separated from gumminess and intended moistness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DRY_DIAG and GUM_DIAG separate bake vs formula causes

competency_questions.question: What causes tunneling and toughness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TUNNEL_DIAG maps to overmixing or gas

competency_questions.question: What causes dense, pale, or greasy cupcakes?
What causes a soapy or bitter leavening off-note?
How is a defect mapped across formula/mixing/bake/ingredient axes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the four axis nodes provide the shared lens

competency_questions.question: How are ingredient quality and food-safety hazards screened?
How is a root cause converted into a verified corrective action?
When does food safety override a flavor or texture decision?

glossary.definition: a wet, dense, sticky mouthfeel from an unset or under-gelatinized crumb
large elongated holes in the crumb from overmixing or excess gas
an alkaline soapy/metallic taste from excess or unneutralized baking soda
the ratio of baking soda to acidic ingredients that neutralizes to the target pH
internal set/temperature endpoint confirming structure and egg/dairy safety
firming and moisture redistribution from starch retrogradation over storage
a formula where sugar and liquid weight meet or exceed flour weight for a tender crumb
the stable dispersion of fat and water that carries air and moisture in batter
a gentle rounded top within threshold, not a defect peak or crack

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for cupcake sensory-defect diagnosis grounded in canonical baking-science references (BakeWise, How Baking Works, The Cake Bible, On Food and Cooking) without supplied datasets

nodes.definition: Define a structured sensory rubric scoring appearance, aroma, crumb, moistness, flavor, mouthfeel, and aftertaste so every defect judgment is reproducible.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Anchors all defect diagnosis to a shared, reproducible vocabulary
pros.example: appearance/crumb/moistness graded 1-5 with photo anchors

cons.claim: Untrained panels drift without calibrated reference standards
cons.example: one taster calls 0.6% soda soapy, another calls it fine

failure_modes: conflating moistness with greasiness
scoring without reference anchors
acceptance_tests: each attribute has a defined 1-5 scale with anchors
two assessors agree within one grade on a reference cupcake

nodes.definition: Enumerate the cupcake defect taxonomy (sinking, doming, cracking, dryness, gumminess, dense, pale, tunneling, overflow, soapy/bitter, greasy) with discriminating sensory signatures.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: A discriminating signature set prevents misrouting to the wrong root cause
pros.example: gummy band at base vs uniform dryness are separated early

cons.claim: Co-occurring defects can mask each other
cons.example: sinking plus gumminess both trace to underbake

failure_modes: one symptom mapped to many unrelated defects
ignoring co-occurrence
acceptance_tests: each defect has at least one discriminating signature
defects are mutually exclusive at the signature level
revisit_triggers: a sample fits two defect classes equally

nodes.definition: Establish the target crumb and set-structure baseline (cell uniformity, fineness, springiness) that defines the non-defective reference for the cupcake.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: A crumb baseline lets tunneling and density be measured as deviations
pros.example: fine even cells distinguish good crumb from tunnel holes

cons.claim: Baseline varies by recipe style (high-ratio vs creamed)
cons.example: velvet vs pound require different crumb targets

failure_modes: judging crumb against the wrong style baseline
acceptance_tests: crumb baseline documented with cell-size and springiness anchors

nodes.definition: Diagnose a sunken center to its root cause across overleavening, excess sugar/liquid, underbake, and oven-door shock, then isolate the dominant driver.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Separates structure collapse from never-set center so the fix is targeted
pros.example: wet streak at center implies underbake, not too much soda

cons.claim: Multiple causes co-occur, inflating false attribution
cons.example: over-soda and underbake both sink the crown

failure_modes: blaming leavening when the real cause is underbake
ignoring oven-door shock
acceptance_tests: each candidate cause is checked against a discriminating signature
dominant driver named with evidence
revisit_triggers: sinking persists after the named fix

nodes.definition: Diagnose excessive doming, peaking, or cracking to oven-too-hot, overmixing/gluten, too much leavening, or stiff batter, distinguishing acceptable gentle dome from a defect peak.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Distinguishes a hot oven from gluten toughness as the peak driver
pros.example: sharp cracked peak with set rim points to oven too hot

cons.claim: A gentle dome may be desirable, not a defect
cons.example: trimming a fine dome wastes good cake

failure_modes: treating an acceptable dome as a defect
missing a too-stiff batter
acceptance_tests: defect peak distinguished from acceptable dome by a stated threshold
revisit_triggers: dome shape changes after oven service

nodes.definition: Diagnose dryness to overbake, too little sugar/fat/liquid, too much flour, or staling/moisture loss, separating bake-driven from formula-driven dryness.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Separates an overbaked exterior from a chronically under-sugared formula
pros.example: dry crumb that was moist yesterday implies staling, not formula

cons.claim: Dryness and gumminess can coexist when bake is uneven
cons.example: crusty top, gummy base from one bad bake

failure_modes: adding liquid when the real cause is overbake
ignoring sugar's water-holding role
acceptance_tests: bake-driven vs formula-driven dryness is explicitly separated
revisit_triggers: dryness recurs after the named fix

nodes.definition: Diagnose a gummy or wet dense band to underbake, removed-too-early, excess liquid/sugar, or insufficient starch gelatinization, separating it from intended moistness.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Distinguishes desirable moistness from an unset gummy band
pros.example: a 1cm wet band at base points to underbake/early pull

cons.claim: Gumminess overlaps with sinking when center never sets
cons.example: both stem from an underbaked core

failure_modes: calling a gummy band 'extra moist' and shipping it
raising sugar without checking doneness
acceptance_tests: internal doneness verified before formula is blamed
gummy band distinguished from intended moistness
revisit_triggers: gumminess recurs at the same oven position

nodes.definition: Diagnose tunneling and toughness to overmixing/gluten development or excess leavening gas, distinguishing large tunnels from fine even crumb.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Links vertical tunnels and rubbery bite to gluten overdevelopment
pros.example: elongated holes plus chew imply overmixed flour

cons.claim: Tunnels from gas escape can mimic mixing tunnels
cons.example: over-soda can also tunnel without overmixing

failure_modes: reducing leavening when overmixing is the real cause
acceptance_tests: tunnel pattern compared against crumb baseline before attribution

nodes.definition: Diagnose dense or pale cupcakes to insufficient leavening/aeration, low oven temperature, or low sugar/soda browning, distinguishing density from paleness causes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Separates a heavy crumb from a merely under-browned surface
pros.example: pale but light crumb points to low oven, not low leavening

cons.claim: Dense and pale can share a single low-heat cause
cons.example: cool oven yields both dense and pale

failure_modes: adding soda for color and triggering a soapy off-note
acceptance_tests: density cause and paleness cause are stated separately

nodes.definition: Diagnose batter overflow and mushroom-tops to overfilled cups, too much leavening, or low-viscosity batter, setting the fill-level and viscosity targets.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Pins overflow to a controllable fill/viscosity target
pros.example: 2/3-fill rule stops mushroom tops

cons.claim: Reducing leavening to curb overflow can flatten rise
cons.example: cutting soda removes overflow but also lift

failure_modes: overfilling then blaming leavening
acceptance_tests: fill-level target documented as a fraction of cup volume

nodes.definition: Diagnose a soapy, metallic, or bitter off-flavor to excess or unneutralized baking soda, wrong soda:acid balance, or undissolved leavening, and confirm against a leavening reference.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Traces an alkaline off-note to a measurable soda:acid imbalance
pros.example: soapy aftertaste plus dark crumb implies unneutralized soda

cons.claim: Bitterness can also come from over-dark bake, not soda
cons.example: Maillard bitterness mimics a soda note

failure_modes: raising soda for browning and creating a soapy taste
leaving soda pockets from poor mixing
acceptance_tests: soda:acid balance recomputed and compared to neutral target
off-note distinguished from over-bake bitterness

nodes.definition: Diagnose a greasy mouthfeel or oily liner to broken emulsion, excess fat, or too-low oven heat that fails to set structure before fat renders.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Links an oily liner to a broken emulsion or excess fat
pros.example: fat ring on liner implies emulsion broke during mixing

cons.claim: Reducing fat to fix grease can dry the crumb
cons.example: cutting butter removes grease but also tenderness

failure_modes: mistaking moistness for grease
acceptance_tests: emulsion integrity assessed before fat ratio is cut
revisit_triggers: greasiness recurs at correct fat ratio

nodes.definition: Assess the formula balance axis (flour:sugar:liquid:fat, soda:acid) as a root-cause lens shared by sinking, dryness, gumminess, soapy, and greasy defects.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: One balance lens explains many defects at once
pros.example: excess sugar both sinks and over-tenderizes

cons.claim: Changing one ratio shifts several attributes simultaneously
cons.example: more liquid fixes dryness but invites gumminess

failure_modes: changing two ratios at once and losing attribution
acceptance_tests: only one formula variable changed per corrective iteration
revisit_triggers: a ratio change resolves one defect but creates another

nodes.definition: Assess the mixing axis (creaming aeration, overmixing/gluten, emulsion stability, even distribution) as a root-cause lens for tunneling, density, greasy, and soapy defects.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Explains aeration and toughness defects from a single process lens
pros.example: undermixed soda leaves soapy pockets; overmixing toughens

cons.claim: More aeration risks overmixing and toughness
cons.example: whipping longer lifts but can tunnel

failure_modes: attributing a mixing fault to the formula
acceptance_tests: mixing change isolated from formula change in any test bake
revisit_triggers: defect tracks with a specific mixer or operator

nodes.definition: Assess the bake axis (oven temperature accuracy, time, position, doneness endpoint) as a root-cause lens for sinking, doming, dryness, gumminess, dense, and pale defects.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: A miscalibrated oven explains many defects before any formula change
pros.example: a 20C-cool oven yields dense, pale, gummy at once

cons.claim: Raising heat to set faster can crack and dry the top
cons.example: hotter oven cures gumminess but cracks the dome

failure_modes: never verifying actual oven temperature with a thermometer
acceptance_tests: oven temperature verified by independent thermometer before formula blame
revisit_triggers: defect correlates with oven rack position

nodes.definition: Assess the ingredient axis (flour protein, leavening freshness/potency, fat type, egg/dairy freshness) as a root-cause lens, including food-safety screening of raw egg and dairy.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Stale or low-potency leavening explains dense/pale before process blame
pros.example: old baking powder yields a flat dense crumb

cons.claim: High-protein flour toughens but is sometimes the only stock on hand
cons.example: bread flour tightens crumb if substituted

failure_modes: ignoring spoiled dairy or raw-egg hazard while chasing texture
acceptance_tests: leavening potency verified
egg/dairy freshness and safety screen recorded before tasting

nodes.definition: Convert a confirmed root cause into a single-variable corrective action, re-bake, and re-score, iterating until the defect clears without creating a new one.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Single-variable changes preserve attribution and converge fast
pros.example: cut soda 25% only, re-bake, confirm off-note gone

cons.claim: Multiple simultaneous changes destroy the cause-effect link
cons.example: changing oven and recipe together hides which worked

failure_modes: changing several variables at once
not re-scoring against the rubric
acceptance_tests: exactly one variable changed per iteration
re-score recorded against the original rubric
revisit_triggers: a fix resolves one defect but introduces another

nodes.definition: Enforce a food-safety gate (egg/dairy doneness, temperature danger zone, allergen control) that overrides any flavor or texture decision when a hazard is present.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: A hard safety gate prevents shipping an underbaked or contaminated cupcake
pros.example: wet center failing egg doneness is held regardless of taste

cons.claim: Holding for safety can reject otherwise pleasant-tasting samples
cons.example: a moist-preferred crumb is rejected if under safe temp

failure_modes: overriding safety to chase moistness
ignoring allergen cross-contact
acceptance_tests: internal temperature meets egg/dairy doneness threshold
allergen cross-contact controls verified

nodes.definition: Design a storage protocol (cooling, wrapping, ambient vs refrigerated, staling control) that protects fresh texture and flavor over the intended shelf life.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Proper wrap and cooling slow staling and protect moistness
pros.example: cool fully then seal to trap moisture without sogging

cons.claim: Refrigeration extends safety but accelerates starch staling
cons.example: fridge keeps dairy safe but dries the crumb

failure_modes: sealing while warm and causing sogginess or mold
refrigerating when staling is the bigger risk
acceptance_tests: cooling-before-sealing step documented
storage mode chosen against shelf-life and safety target

nodes.definition: Calibrate assessors against reference standards and anchored scales so sensory scores are reproducible across tasters and sessions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Calibration keeps defect scores comparable across days and tasters
pros.example: all assessors score the reference soapy note alike

cons.claim: Calibration takes time and reference materials
cons.example: weekly recalibration costs sessions

failure_modes: drifting scales producing non-comparable scores
acceptance_tests: inter-assessor agreement within one grade on reference samples

nodes.definition: Triage available evidence (sensory signature, formula record, bake log, ingredient lot) to rank candidate root causes before any corrective change.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: defect recurrence pattern or formula change observed

pros.claim: Ranking candidates before acting avoids random fixes
pros.example: check oven temp first when dense+pale+gummy co-occur

cons.claim: Triage can over-anchor on the first plausible cause
cons.example: fixating on soda when oven is the real fault

failure_modes: acting on the first guess without cross-checking records
acceptance_tests: at least two candidate causes ranked with discriminating evidence
revisit_triggers: top candidate fix fails to resolve the defect

edges.risk_of_conflict: formula changed for a storage issue

edges.why_related: fixing dryness by adding liquid can cause gumminess
edges.example: more liquid cures dryness but risks a gummy band
edges.resolution_rule: verify doneness first; adjust bake before liquid so moistness rises without an unset band

edges.why_related: more aeration improves rise but overmixing tunnels
edges.example: extra whipping lifts but can tunnel
edges.resolution_rule: mix to just-combined target; prefer leavening over extra mixing when more lift is needed

edges.why_related: adding soda for browning can create a soapy note
edges.example: more soda browns but tastes soapy
edges.resolution_rule: hold soda at neutral soda:acid; achieve color via bake temperature, not extra soda

edges.why_related: cutting fat to fix grease can dry the crumb
edges.example: less butter removes grease but dries crumb
edges.resolution_rule: repair the emulsion before cutting fat; reduce fat only if emulsion is sound and grease persists

edges.why_related: safety hold can override a taste-driven corrective change
edges.risk_of_conflict: shipping an unsafe sample for taste
edges.example: wet center fails egg doneness despite preferred moistness
edges.resolution_rule: safety gate dominates: hold the sample until doneness and allergen controls pass, regardless of flavor

edges.why_related: ambient storage protects texture but may risk dairy safety
edges.example: ambient keeps crumb fresh but dairy filling needs cold
edges.resolution_rule: safety gate dominates: refrigerate when a perishable filling is present even at a texture cost

edges.why_related: ingredient screening must pass the safety gate
edges.resolution_rule: safety screen must pass before ingredient is used in any diagnostic bake

edges.why_related: triage output orders the corrective loop
an underbaked core can present as both sinking and gumminess

conflict_axes.trigger: raising moisture to avoid dryness softens structure toward gumminess or sinking
resolution_order: add liquid only if structure holds
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if a gummy band or sink appears, structure side dominates and bake is corrected before adding moisture
conflict_axes.example: extra milk fixes dryness but center sinks

conflict_axes.trigger: more sugar/fat tenderizes but can weaken rise or, with overmixing, peak and tunnel
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if peaking or tunneling appears, rise/structure side dominates and mixing is shortened
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: peak height exceeds acceptable dome threshold
conflict_axes.example: extra fat tenderizes but flattens rise

conflict_axes.trigger: raising sugar boosts perceived sweetness but can flatten aroma and flavor complexity
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if flavor complexity score drops, flavor side dominates and sweetness is held
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: flavor complexity grade drops by one
conflict_axes.example: more sugar masks vanilla and salt notes

conflict_axes.trigger: a sweet frosting plus a sweet crumb pushes total sweetness past balance
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if combined sweetness exceeds target, the crumb sugar is reduced first to preserve frosting role
conflict_axes.example: sweet buttercream over sweet cake cloys

conflict_axes.trigger: skipping re-score or calibration to save time degrades diagnostic quality
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: quality gates dominate: no fix is accepted without a rubric re-score

conflict_axes.trigger: ambient storage keeps texture fresh but shortens safe shelf life; refrigeration extends it but stales
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if shelf-life target is unmet, shelf-life side dominates and storage mode is chosen for it
conflict_axes.example: fridge extends life but dries crumb

conflict_axes.trigger: a flavor or texture preference conflicts with a doneness, danger-zone, or allergen requirement
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: safety side always dominates; held until doneness and allergen controls pass

conflict_axes.trigger: adding soda to deepen browning can introduce a soapy or bitter alkaline note
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if a soapy off-note appears, flavor side dominates and soda is returned to neutral
conflict_axes.example: more soda darkens crumb but tastes soapy

conflict_axes.trigger: more mixing aerates and lifts but overdevelops gluten into toughness and tunnels
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if tunneling or chew appears, structure side dominates and mixing is shortened
conflict_axes.example: longer mix lifts but toughens crumb

edge_cases.trigger: sinking and gumminess co-occur from one underbake
edge_cases.failure_mode: two defects logged as two causes, doubling the fix
edge_cases.example: wet center both sinks and gums
edge_cases.detection_method: internal-temperature probe to confirm a single unset core

edge_cases.trigger: a gentle dome is flagged as a defect
edge_cases.failure_mode: good cake trimmed or recipe changed needlessly
edge_cases.detection_method: compare dome height to the acceptable-dome threshold

edge_cases.trigger: oven temperature never verified before formula blame
edge_cases.failure_mode: formula changed to fix a miscalibrated oven
edge_cases.example: dense+pale traced to a 20C-cool oven, not the recipe
edge_cases.detection_method: independent oven thermometer reading vs set point

edge_cases.trigger: leavening potency not checked on a dense bake
edge_cases.failure_mode: process blamed while baking powder is dead
edge_cases.example: old powder yields a flat dense crumb
edge_cases.detection_method: water-fizz potency test on the leavening lot

edge_cases.trigger: a gummy unset band is called extra moist and shipped
edge_cases.example: wet basal band fails egg doneness

edge_cases.trigger: two variables changed in one corrective iteration
edge_cases.example: oven and recipe changed together hide which worked
edge_cases.detection_method: diff the corrective record for change count

edge_cases.trigger: soda raised to fix paleness creates a soapy note
edge_cases.failure_mode: color gained at the cost of flavor
edge_cases.detection_method: taste-check aftertaste after a soda change

edge_cases.example: two tasters disagree two grades on soapiness
edge_cases.detection_method: inter-assessor agreement check on a reference sample

edge_cases.failure_mode: trapped steam causes sogginess or mold
edge_cases.example: warm-sealed cupcakes sweat inside the wrap

edge_cases.trigger: a candidate cause references a defect not in taxonomy
edge_cases.failure_mode: diagnosis routed to a non-existent class
edge_cases.example: a cause cites 'rubbery-pale' which is not a defined defect
edge_cases.detection_method: reference resolver over candidate-cause defect ids
resolution: map to a real defect class
or add the class to taxonomy

edge_cases.trigger: an allergen substitution introduced without cross-contact control
edge_cases.failure_mode: allergen exposure risk in a shared line
edge_cases.example: nut flour swapped in without line cleaning
edge_cases.detection_method: allergen control checklist on the new ingredient

edge_cases.trigger: cups overfilled then leavening blamed for overflow
edge_cases.example: mushroom tops from filling cups too full
edge_cases.detection_method: fill-weight check against the fill-level target
